Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

OPENS Ch 11: 'HERMON AND HER WALLS HAVE FALLEN; for God has repaid them according to their wickedness' — the chapter explicitly names TYRE AND SIDON as the typological-source for Ṣiruṣaydan's name. Per Horovitz 1905 p. 195 fn. 3 + Dillmann LEXICON LINGUAE AETHIOPICAE (1865, the originator of the etymology): **Ṣiruṣaydan = Ṣir-uṣ-Aydan = TYRE + SIDON** (the Phoenician-coastal cities, joined by the conjunction). Tyre + Sidon are the canonical BIBLICAL-TYPE for arrogant maritime-commercial pride (Ezekiel 26-28 prophecies; Isaiah 23 burden-of-Tyre; Joel 3:4-8). The villain-name is a TYPOLOGICAL CIPHER for the arrogant-imperial-city-state rather than historical-king identification. The chapter prophesies Tyre+Sidon's eschatological-shame at resurrection (11:3 — 'at the resurrection, the shame of Jerusalem shall be revealed'); Jerusalem and Tyre+Sidon are both judged by the same divine-criterion (covenant-faithfulness).

TIER-2 AUDIT INTEGRATION (γ.4.8.F) — HOROVITZ FN-3 CROSS-REFERENCE LIST CORRECTED. Per TIER2_AUDIT.md §2 Finding 2, the Horovitz 1905 p. 194 footnote 3 cross-reference list — as transcribed in the earlier SOURCES.md as 'X 3, XI 9, XV 7/8/9, XXVI 10, XXVIII 4/5, XXX 1, XXXI 2, XXXII 1' — is corrected by the direct Wright-catalogue examination to the seven confirmed Geʽez-Meqabyan entries: **X 3, XI 9, XV 7, XXVI 10, XXVIII 5, XXXI 2, XXXII 1** (plus the Vulgate-translation Maccabees items XV 8-9 and XXVIII 4 noted separately as the parallel later translation, NOT the Geʽez Meqabyan). The previously-cited 'XXX 1' is dropped as an unverifiable OCR transcription artifact — Wright's entry XXX (Orient. 829*, f. 7) is a small two-leaf fragment containing ONLY MICAH 7:17-20 + JOEL 1:1-3:21, with no Maccabees material whatsoever. Horovitz, working directly from the printed catalogue, would not have cited the Micah/Joel fragment as a Maccabees witness. The corrected list is the apparatus's authoritative Geʽez-Meqabyan-MS-roster.
